independent_outcomes: Core cross-wave hold: a fold conflict whose head merges cleanly onto the base and that _clash/_partners attributes to one or more single bundles already on the line (in-batch earlier wave, or carried finished heads fed into the partner set) is held like held_conflict, naming those partners, and the run goes on. Covers cases (1), (2) and (5): the case-5 flip, including the 'partner is your own prerequisite, rebuild on its branch' wording, is the same hold seen from a dependent. Test: cases 1, 2, 5 plus the unchanged base-taken-in stop.

Joint ('together') attribution: when no single bundle explains the clash, name exactly the bundles that cause it jointly (the leave-one-out rule, kept outside _clash) and never unrelated line bundles, including when direct and joint clashes share a file or several joint clashes coexist. Covers case (4) plus the iteration-1/2/3 probes (unrelated X named; probe-joint; probe-same-file). Without it, the core hold can keep stopping the run, as today, when no single partner is found.

Stranded-by-moved-base diagnosis: tell 'the partner on the line no longer merges onto the base that head actually holds' apart from an ordinary overlap, aim the fix at the partner's owner (rebuild on the new <remote>/main) without blaming the held bundle, and keep Conflicts-with partners of that hold from getting the opposite advice. Covers case (3) and most of the iteration-2/3 rejections (merge-base vs current tip, a double main move, main undoing a commit, the X Conflicts-with message). Needs #738 on the base. Without it, the core hold can treat a partner that fails _trial(base, [partner]) as a line failure and stop, as today.
proposed_seams: Cut between the core single-partner hold and the stranded diagnosis. In the core child, any partner whose own head fails to merge onto the base stays a STOPPING line failure (today's behaviour, so never wrong advice). The stranded child then turns that stop into a partner-aimed hold. This is the seam that matters most: iterations 2 and 3 were rejected mostly on stranded-check findings (which base to trial against, whether the base move is really the cause, the wording for Conflicts-with partners). That is a separate diagnosis problem with its own fixture (#738 required, main moved mid-run), and it now holds back the in-batch and carried-finished holds, which iteration 1 already showed work.

Cut between the core hold and the joint/'together' fallback. In the core child, a clash that no single bundle explains stays a stop. The joint child adds leave-one-out naming in the fold's classification, next to _held_by. It has its own success criterion ('names exactly the joint causes, never an unrelated line bundle') and its own probes from iterations 1-3. It touches the same fold branch as the core, so it should ship after the core, not alongside it.

Not a seam: cases (1), (2) and the case-(5) flip share one rule and one code path (the fold's conflict branch + _clash/_partners + feeding held_conflict into _runnable). Carried finished heads are only a widened partner set. Keep them together.

Ordering if split: core -> {joint, stranded} (the last two are independent of each other; both extend the core's classification). Only the stranded child needs Depends on: 738 for its fixture. The core still edits the held sets/_runnable call in flow.py that #738 touches, so it keeps the dependency for conflict reasons.
